turns.text:
Built and verified. The corridor occupies columns 10–50:

- **Columns 10–11:** mini portal (`N`) then ball portal (`B`) at floor level.
- **Row 4:** solid ceiling running the whole length — free space is rows 1–3 (y 0–120).
- **Spikes:** five on the ceiling (cols 15, 24, 32, 40, 48) and four on the floor (cols 20, 28, 36, 44), alternating so the ball has to flip each time.
- **Columns 50–51:** cube portal (`C`) then normal-size portal (`n`).

The section leads with a **ceiling** spike so the ball gets a free stretch at the start — my first attempt put a floor spike first, and the solver showed the only way through was a cube jump into the ball portal with an 8 ms (2-tick) window, which is effectively frame-perfect. Reordering it fixed that.

**Playability:** verified with the game's physics — `possible`. Eight flips, each with a ~104–116 ms timing window (comfortable; nothing frame-perfect). The route exits at x≈1860 as a normal-size cube on the ground with normal gravity, so the ending is clean.

Not done: decoration, and the level has no start position or speed portal — it starts as a cube at 1x by default, which is what the section assumes. I left the view at the section entrance. Want me to playtest it in the editor?
